editorial.summary: A 1:48 Kevin Smith-titled excerpt about caring for Mulder, a large yellow Lab who could no longer use his hind legs and had recently died. While supporting Mulder with a scarf sling and waiting for a slow elevator, the speaker repeatedly studied a painting he says David Choe gave him. Initial graphic interest became a year-long practice of noticing new details and inventing different stories; he reports that the painting made difficult early mornings better. That is personal testimony, not clinical evidence. Mulder, yellow Lab, Choe’s painting and dumbwaiter are repaired. A likely “our podcast” phrase retains residual uncertainty. The source term “crippled,” care mechanics, profanity masks and grief remain uncensored. The final “his art works like a…” is clipped and not completed. The title attributes Kevin Smith at source level, but captions do not label turns; zero named turns ship.
